key_insight: PsychFound is a psychiatry-specialized LLM fine-tuned on expert knowledge and clinical records that achieves clinical-grade performance and improves diagnostic and treatment decision-making when integrated into clinical workflows.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between general-purpose LLMs and psychiatry practice by providing a domain-adapted model that reliably supports clinicians with specialist knowledge and case-based reasoning.
method: Domain adaptation: fine-tune a large pretrained language model on curated psychiatric expert texts and de-identified clinical records.
Clinical evaluation: benchmark model outputs against clinical-grade standards and clinician assessments to validate diagnostic and treatment recommendations.
Workflow integration: deploy model as decision-support tools within clinician workflows to augment diagnosis, treatment planning, and documentation.
impact: Demonstrates that targeted domain adaptation yields clinically actionable LLMs for specialty care, offering a template for building safe, evaluated AI assistants in healthcare while highlighting the need for rigorous validation and privacy safeguards.
visual_elements: Data-to-model flowchart showing sources (expert guidelines, case records) → fine-tuning → PsychFound
Bar/line chart comparing PsychFound vs. baseline LLMs on clinical-grade metrics (diagnosis accuracy, treatment concordance)
Clinical workflow diagram illustrating how the model interfaces with clinician decision steps (assessment → suggestion → clinician review)
Icon stack for governance: privacy, safety, and evaluation checks (to indicate ethical/validation layers)
paper_title: A domain-adapted large language model to support clinicians in psychiatric clinical practice
paper_authors: Ruoxi Wang, Shuyu Liu, Ling Zhang, Xuequan Zhu, Zhi Yang
